turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that, and on what basis.
Can I ask something off the record?
There's no off the record with me, Hale. Anything you say in this room goes on my pad. You still haven't told me who entered that zero.
When was the last time you actually sat with him while he did homework?

My parenting isn't what's on the table, Hale, your process is. I'm writing down that your first answer about Owen's zero was a question about my kitchen table. Now tell me who entered it and whether anyone spoke to Owen before they did.
Because in my experience, kids who cheat have parents who are too busy to notice.

You just put Owen and "kids who cheat" in the same sentence, and then told me I'm "too busy to notice." My son doesn't lie, and I don't appreciate being told what kind of mother I am by someone who couldn't pick up a phone. I'm writing that down word for word, and it's going upstairs to the principal with me today.
